razonamiento: The architecture diagram shows an acoustic water leak detection pipeline from Mueller Water Products. IoT-enabled fire hydrants send acoustic data to API Gateway, which stores the files in S3. A batch process running on ECS retrieves the data from S3 to compute acoustic correlations, then invokes a SageMaker endpoint to score leak probabilities. The score is provided to human analysts for review.
nombre: Mueller Water Products Intelligent Water Platform

nodes.name: Fire Hydrant
nodes.notes: Records acoustic signals on the pipe network

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Runs processor-intensive correlation algorithms across node pairs

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: ML endpoint assigning leak probabilities to persistent correlations

nodes.name: Analyst
nodes.notes: Reviews leak scores and persistent correlations to qualify leaks

edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow from fire hydrant to API Gateway and spoken: 'Those files are pushed through API gateway on a daily basis.'
Drawn arrow from API Gateway to S3 and spoken: 'those files are then pushed and persisted in S3.'

edges.notes: Retrieves files for daily batch correlation processing
edges.respaldo: Drawn curved arrow from S3 to ECS and spoken: 'The next process that kicks off is a batch process that occurs on a daily basis where each of the files is processed as a node pair... And that happens in ECS.'

edges.notes: Sends persistent correlations for ML inference
edges.respaldo: Drawn arrow from ECS to SageMaker and spoken: 'These persistent correlations are then further classified using a SageMaker ML endpoint that will assign a probability to that persistent correlation.'

edges.notes: Delivers leak score probability for manual review
edges.respaldo: Spoken: 'So from the SageMaker endpoint, we get a leak score, a probability, and then we feed that to our human analyst team who will further classify that leak.'
